question: Does the existing shed roof stay on shoring and get reintegrated, or is a new gable/hip roof now contracted?
why_it_matters: A new roof replaces the shoring-through-framing sequence with roof framing, sheathing and roofing tasks and adds a truss/rafter procurement.
unblocks: Shoring vs new-roof-framing task chain, roofing procurement, framing inspection scope

choices: Existing shed roof retained and reintegrated (per proposal)
New gable roof replaces existing
New hip roof replaces existing
Undecided — customer still reviewing presentation

question: Are Option 1 upsized 24x24x12 footers and brick pier wraps now contracted, or does the base 12x12x12 footer stand?
why_it_matters: Footer size must be right before the pour; brick wrap adds a masonry phase after posts are set.
unblocks: Footer excavation and concrete quantities, masonry phase inclusion, brick procurement

choices: No — base 12x12x12 footers, bare posts
Yes — 24x24x12 footers plus brick wrap on all posts
Footers upsized only, no brick
Undecided

question: Are the post footers saw-cut through the existing concrete pad or dug in soil beside it?
why_it_matters: Saw-cutting adds a concrete saw, extra labor and possible pad demolition the breakdown does not carry.
unblocks: Footer excavation task method, equipment, duration

choices: Dug in soil adjacent to the pad
Saw-cut through the existing pad
Mix — some in pad, some in soil
Unknown until site visit

question: How does the new floor bear at the house side: ledger on the existing wall, a second post row, or existing house framing?
why_it_matters: A ledger on brick, an inner post line, or existing framing each produce different foundation and floor-framing tasks.
unblocks: Floor framing task list, footer count, ledger hardware procurement

choices: Ledger bolted to the existing house wall
Beam on a second (inner) post row
Bears on existing house rim/framing
Engineer or field verification to determine

question: Is the house-side wall furred and drywalled over brick, left as exposed brick, or framed as a full 2x4 insulated wall?
why_it_matters: Determines whether 344 SF of drywall, furring, or a fourth framed wall belongs in the plan.
unblocks: Wall framing quantity, furring task, drywall and insulation scope on the house side

choices: Furring strips plus drywall over brick
Exposed brick — no drywall on that wall
Full 2x4 framed and insulated wall in front of brick

question: Which opening schedule governs ordering: proposal 6x 36x60 + one 36x80 door, or presentation 7 windows + a double door?
why_it_matters: Window count, 5050 units and a house-wall double door change headers, rough openings and lead times.
unblocks: Window/door procurement, header framing, brick-wall opening work

choices: Proposal schedule (6 x 36x60, one 36x80 door)
Presentation p.4 schedule (4x3050, 2x5050, 1x3036, 3068 + 6568 double)
Hybrid — customer to finalize before ordering

question: Are the exterior deck, railing, and stairs to grade shown in the renders contracted work?
why_it_matters: A deck and stairs add footers, framing, railing and a separate inspection the proposal does not carry.
unblocks: Deck-build phase inclusion, additional footer count, railing procurement

choices: No — not in scope
Yes — deck with railing and stairs
Stairs only
Deck only, no stairs

question: Is Option 2 interior finish (LVP, baseboard, casing, primer and paint) now contracted?
why_it_matters: Adds flooring, trim and two paint phases and pushes material-selection gates onto the schedule.
unblocks: Interior finish phase inclusion, flooring/trim/paint procurement

choices: No — base drywall-ready only
Yes — full Option 2
Partial (specify items)

question: Is ceiling drywall and roof/ceiling-cavity insulation part of this job?
why_it_matters: The proposal demolishes the ceiling but finishes walls only; a ceiling adds insulation and drywall tasks before fixtures.
unblocks: Insulation and drywall task scope, fixture install sequencing

choices: No — walls only per proposal
Yes — insulate and drywall the ceiling
Ceiling drywall only, no insulation
Insulation only, no ceiling drywall

question: What is the intended construction start window, given data.json shows 2026-03-01, which has passed?
why_it_matters: Foundation and framing cannot fall in the mid-Dec to mid-Feb window and the plan needs a real anchor date.
unblocks: Plan start date and winter-window placement of foundation/framing

choices: Fall 2026 (Oct–Nov)
Late Feb / March 2027 after the winter window
Immediately (Sept 2026)
Unscheduled — awaiting deposit or selections

question: Can equipment (lift, trailer, mixer) reach the ground beneath the elevated sunroom on the sloped lot?
why_it_matters: Hand-carry access changes demo lowering, footer, soffit and siding durations and the equipment list.
unblocks: Equipment selection, elevated-work durations, debris handling method

choices: Yes — drive-around access to the rear
Hand-carry / wheelbarrow only
Partial — trailer to side yard, hand-carry under the structure
Unknown until site visit

question: Does any existing equipment or line (fused disconnect, meter, hose bib, vents) need relocating off the sunroom before demo?
why_it_matters: A relocation is a separate pre-demo work package with an electrician on the critical path.
unblocks: checklist item utility_relocations (Utility & equipment relocations (heat pump, disconnect, lines))

choices: No — disconnect stays in place and is reused after conversion
Yes — fused disconnect must be moved or temp-powered during demo
Yes — other equipment (hose bib, vent, line set) sits in the footprint
Unknown until electrician assesses the disconnect

question: Are the customer's final material selections (siding profile/color, windows, door, mini-split, fixtures) made?
why_it_matters: Canon forbids scheduling before selections; unselected allowances push the demo start and every order date.
unblocks: checklist item site_and_structure_demo (Demolition (site + structure at addition footprint))

choices: No — selections still open on all allowances
Partially — siding and openings picked, mini-split/fixtures open
Yes — all selections made and documented

question: Is the temporary roof shoring an in-house design, or does it need an engineer's stamp before demo?
why_it_matters: An engineered shoring design adds a lead time ahead of demo that the plan must carry.
unblocks: checklist item site_prep (Site prep (protection, staging, access))

choices: In-house design — shoring materials only
Engineer-stamped shoring design required (1-3 weeks lead)
AHJ decides at permit review

question: Are the vinyl windows and exterior door stock sizes or custom order?
why_it_matters: Stock lands in 2-3 weeks; custom runs 4-6 and sets how early the order must precede demo.

choices: Stock — 36x60 vinyl DH and 36x80 pre-hung door off the shelf
Custom — sized to field-measured rough openings after framing
Mixed — stock door, custom windows

question: When is the vinyl soffit under the floor framing installed?
why_it_matters: Placement decides whether soffit rides the floor-framing task or an underside task needing lift/scaffold access.

choices: From below after joists, alongside siding
Before joists are set, from above
After subfloor, from scaffolding under the deck

question: Are the window headers built-up dimensional lumber or LVL?
why_it_matters: LVL headers add a separate engineered-lumber order the framing package does not cover.

choices: Built-up 2x dimensional — no LVL on the job
LVL headers at the six window openings
Engineer/plan reviewer decides

question: Where does the mini-split condenser sit: ground pad below, or wall bracket on the new structure?
why_it_matters: Location sets line-set length, disconnect placement, and whether ground access below the elevated room is needed.
unblocks: checklist item rough_hvac (Rough HVAC (line set / duct extension))

choices: Ground pad on or near the existing slab below
Wall bracket on the new exterior wall
Undecided until mini-split is selected
